## 💡 Project Ideas

### Project 1: FX Hedge Ratio Advisor
**Pitch:** An agentic copilot that tells treasury desks and fund managers exactly how much FX exposure to hedge — and explains why — in plain English.

**Problem:** FX hedging decisions at most firms live in a trader's head or a static Excel model. There is no tool that continuously ingests spot rates, carry data, and portfolio NAV, then surfaces an actionable hedge recommendation with a written rationale a risk committee can sign off on.

**Stack:** Python (pandas, numpy, scipy) · yfinance / Alpha Vantage for spot/forward rates · FRED API for interest rate differentials · Claude Haiku 4.5 for narrative generation · Streamlit for UI · Supabase (optional) for logging recommendations over time

**Build time:** 3–4 days MVP; +1 day for PDF memo export

**Audience:** FX desks, treasury functions, multi-family offices, IM recruiters — directly validates Afterprime day-job at investor-grade level.

**LinkedIn angle:** "I spent 18 months managing FX hedge books manually. I built a tool that automates the carry-adjusted optimal hedge ratio calculation and drafts the committee memo in under 30 seconds. Here is what that looks like for AUD/USD exposure."

**Difficulty:** MEDIUM

---

### Project 2: Earnings Intelligence Pipeline
**Pitch:** A research analyst that never sleeps — ingests every earnings call transcript and 10-Q for a watchlist, then delivers a CFA-style investment memo to your inbox within minutes of filing.

**Problem:** Buy-side analysts spend 60–70% of their time on information gathering and first-draft synthesis, not on actual judgement. A junior analyst or aspiring PM building toward their own fund cannot afford a Bloomberg Terminal or a research team.

**Stack:** Python · SEC EDGAR full-text search API (free) · Whisper API or Rev.ai for earnings call audio transcription · Claude Sonnet 4.6 for memo quality · yfinance for price/valuation context · Jinja2 for memo templating · Resend / Gmail API for delivery · GitHub Actions or cron for triggers

**Build time:** 4–5 days (budget a full day for prompt engineering the memo to CFA standard)

**Audience:** Equity research recruiters, long/short hedge funds, VC associates, any hiring manager who asks "how do you form a view on a company?"

**LinkedIn angle:** "I wanted to build toward running my own fund but could not generate research at institutional quality without a team. So I built one. This pipeline produced a 4-page investment memo on NVDA earnings in 8 minutes — including transcript sentiment, FCF delta, and a bear/base/bull NAV range."

**Difficulty:** MEDIUM

---

### Project 3: Multi-Asset Drawdown Sentinel
**Pitch:** A real-time portfolio risk monitor that catches tail events before they become margin calls — and explains the regime shift in the language of a CFA charterholder, not a quant.

**Problem:** Most retail and emerging fund managers track P&L but not risk-adjusted drawdown in real time. By the time a position is hurting, the correlated regime shift happened two days ago. This tool watches correlations, VaR, and max drawdown continuously and fires a plain-English alert the moment the portfolio is behaving outside its historical risk envelope.

**Stack:** Python (numpy, scipy, cvxpy) · yfinance for daily/intraday prices across equities, FX, crypto · Claude Haiku 4.5 for narrative alert generation · Plotly Dash or Streamlit for live dashboard · Telegram Bot API for push alerts · Supabase to log risk snapshots over time

**Build time:** 5 days total (3 core + 1 alerts + 1 stress test tab)

**Audience:** Fund-of-funds allocators evaluating emerging managers, family offices, crypto desks (directly maps to Afterprime's crypto/hedging scope). Each module maps to CAIA L2 and CFA L2 curriculum directly.

**LinkedIn angle:** "Running your own capital means knowing your risk before your broker does. I built a sentinel that watches five asset classes simultaneously, detects correlation regime breaks, and sends me a two-paragraph risk brief via Telegram. It flagged the August carry unwind three hours before my positions were touched."

**Difficulty:** HARD

### Total Cost if All 3 Built

Building all three projects requires approximately 104 hours to MVP and 140 hours to portfolio-ready across the three tools. Combined monthly API costs run ~$38/month (dominated by Whisper transcription) or ~$5.50/month if using text-only filings for the Earnings Pipeline. Optional hosting on Render adds $7/month per service if Streamlit Community Cloud doesn't fit the use case.

### Recommendation

Start with the **FX Hedge Ratio Advisor** this week. It is the fastest to ship (3.5 days), costs less than $1/month to run, directly maps to your current role at Afterprime (strengthening the 482/186 visa case by demonstrating specialised skill contribution in writing), and gives you a LinkedIn post within 7 days. The carry-adjusted optimal hedge ratio is a specific, defensible methodology — not a tutorial — and framing it as "I automate my own job's committee workflow" is a stronger signal than any generic AI project.

The **Earnings Intelligence Pipeline** is the highest-leverage career move for breaking into investment management or VC. Build it second and stake it on a real company you have a genuine view on — the memo quality will make or break the impression, so spend the prompt-engineering day. The **Drawdown Sentinel** is the fund-raising capstone: build it when you are 6–12 months from needing to demo to allocators. All three can share a single `ai-finance-tools` GitHub repo with a clean README — that repo link is what you drop in every application.

### Cost Optimization Tips

- **Use Haiku 4.5 for Projects 1 and 3** — the outputs are structured/formulaic enough that the quality gap vs Sonnet is negligible, and costs drop 4–5×.
- **Skip Whisper for the Earnings Pipeline v1** — SEC EDGAR text filings are free and high-quality; add audio transcription only once the text-only version is proving its value.
- **Cache frequent context** — Anthropic's 75% cache-read discount (as of Fable 5.1) means system prompts, rubrics, and boilerplate memo templates should all be cache-eligible to cut 70%+ off steady-state cost.
